site.name: Wellington Mine
overview: The Wellington was one of the major hard-rock mining operations in French Gulch east of Breckenridge. Historically separate from the neighboring Oro Mine, the two properties were combined in 1907 as the Wellington-Oro complex.
The operation is especially useful for understanding changes in mining and milling technology, with extensive underground workings and several generations of ore-processing equipment.

timeline.text: Major lode-mining activity developed in French Gulch, including the Wellington and Oro properties.
The previously separate Wellington and Oro mines were combined into the Wellington-Oro operation.
A gravity mill was built to concentrate ore.
A roasting and magnetic-separation plant was constructed for zinc-ore treatment.
Flotation technology replaced the older roasting and magnetic-separation process.
The earlier gravity mill ceased operation.
Mining activity continued intermittently after the main historic production period.
Treatment facilities address contaminated water draining from historic workings.

moreHistory: EPA historical studies describe the Wellington-Oro as the largest lode-mining operation in French Gulch, with more than 12 miles of underground workings.
The successive milling systems illustrate how operators adapted to changing ore types and metallurgical technology.
The Wellington and Oro began as separate mines. Their later combination is historically important, but the original identities should not be erased.
Modern remediation is part of the site’s continuing history and has altered portions of the industrial landscape.
